Code reference¶

App configuration¶

Application configuration for the news app.

Registers the app with Django and wires up its signal handlers once the app registry is fully loaded.

class news.apps.NewsConfig(app_name, app_module)[source]¶

Django configuration for the news application.

Sets the default primary key type and the human-readable name shown in the admin, and connects signals when the app is ready.

ready()[source]¶

Connect the app’s signal handlers when Django starts.

Importing the signals module registers its @receiver handlers. The create_role_groups handler is connected to post_migrate so the Reader, Editor and Journalist groups are built after this app’s permissions exist in the database.

Models¶

Data models for the News Application.

Tables (all in third normal form):

  • CustomUser - every account; role decides the user’s group.

  • Publisher - a curated publication with editors and journalists.

  • Article - written by a journalist, optionally for a publisher.

  • Newsletter - a journalist’s curated collection of articles.

  • ApprovedArticleLog - records received by the /api/approved/ endpoint.

Many-to-many relations (subscriptions, publisher staff, newsletter articles) are stored in Django’s automatic join tables, so no column ever holds a list of values.

A user of the news site with exactly one role.

Reader-only fields:

Roles and groups¶

Role definitions and the group/permission set-up that goes with them.

Every user has exactly one role. Each role maps to a Django Group of the same name, and each group is given the model permissions listed in ROLE_PERMISSIONS. Access control throughout the project checks these permissions (user.has_perm(...)) rather than hard-coding role names wherever possible.

news.roles.ensure_role_groups()[source]¶

Create the Reader, Editor and Journalist groups (if missing) and give each one exactly the permissions listed in ROLE_PERMISSIONS.

Safe to run repeatedly. Returns a dict of role -> Group.

news.roles.assign_role_group(user)[source]¶

Put user into the group that matches their role and remove them from the other role groups. Non-role groups are left alone.

Website views¶

Website views.

Access control uses Django’s permission system: each view requires the model permission its action needs (granted through the user’s role group), and journalists can only change their own work.

Parameters:

API permissions¶

REST API permission classes.

Each class checks the Django model permissions that the user’s role group grants (see roles.py), plus ownership rules for journalists.

news.permissions.has_model_perm(user, action, model_name)[source]¶

True if user has e.g. news.change_article.

class news.permissions.RoleModelPermission[source]¶

Bases: BasePermission

Base class for Article and Newsletter permissions.

  • Reading needs view_<model> (all roles have it).

  • Writing needs the matching add/change/delete permission, so: only journalists can create, editors and journalists can update/delete, readers can only view.

  • Journalists may only update/delete their own items; editors may update/delete any.

has_permission(request, view)[source]¶

Check the request against the user’s model permissions.

Parameters:

  • request – The incoming DRF request.

  • view – The view being accessed.

Returns:

True if the user is logged in and holds the permission that matches the HTTP method, otherwise False.

Return type:

bool

has_object_permission(request, view, obj)[source]¶

Apply ownership rules to a single article or newsletter.

Reads are always allowed here. Superusers and editors may change any item; journalists may only change their own.

Parameters:

  • request – The incoming DRF request.

  • view – The view being accessed.

  • obj – The article or newsletter being accessed.

Returns:

True if the user may act on obj.

Return type:

bool

Bases: BasePermission

Allows the request if it carries the shared X-Api-Key header.

Used by POST /api/approved/ so that only this application’s own signal can write to the approval log.

API views¶

REST API views.

Endpoints (all under /api/):

POST token/ obtain an auth token GET articles/ approved articles POST articles/ create (journalists) GET articles/subscribed/ reader’s subscribed content GET articles/pending/ unapproved articles (editors) GET articles/<id>/ one article PUT articles/<id>/ update (editors / own journalist) PATCH articles/<id>/ partial update DELETE articles/<id>/ delete (editors / own journalist) POST articles/<id>/approve/ approve (editors) CRUD newsletters/ newsletters GET publishers/ publishers (read-only) GET users/me/ the logged-in user POST approved/ log an approved article (API key) GET approved/ approval log (editors)

get_queryset()[source]¶

Get the list of items for this view. This must be an iterable, and may be a queryset. Defaults to using self.queryset.

This method should always be used rather than accessing self.queryset directly, as self.queryset gets evaluated only once, and those results are cached for all subsequent requests.

You may want to override this if you need to provide different querysets depending on the incoming request.

(Eg. return a list of items that is specific to the user)

Services¶

Actions performed when an editor approves an article.

Kept separate from signals.py so each unit of work can be called and tested on its own (and mocked in the tests).

news.services.get_subscriber_emails(article)[source]¶

Return a sorted list of unique email addresses for readers who subscribe to the article’s journalist or to its publisher.

news.services.build_article_email(article, recipients)[source]¶

Build (but do not send) the email for an approved article.

news.services.email_subscribers(article)[source]¶

Email an approved article to its subscribers.

Returns the number of recipients emailed (0 if there were none or sending failed). Errors are logged, never raised, so a mail problem cannot undo an editor’s approval.

news.services.build_approved_payload(article)[source]¶

JSON body sent to the /api/approved/ endpoint.

news.services.post_to_approved_endpoint(article)[source]¶

POST the approved article to our own /api/approved/ endpoint using the requests module.

Returns the Response, or None if the request failed. Failures are logged rather than raised.

Signals¶

Signal handlers (implementation strategy: Option 1 - Django signals).

  • pre_save / post_save on Article: when an article changes from “not approved” to “approved”, email subscribers and POST the article to /api/approved/.

  • m2m_changed on reader subscriptions: stop non-readers from holding subscriptions and stop readers subscribing to non-journalists.

  • post_migrate: create the role groups and their permissions.

news.signals.remember_previous_approval(sender, instance, **kwargs)[source]¶

Store whether the article was already approved before this save, so post_save can tell if this save is the approval.

news.signals.handle_article_approval(sender, instance, created, **kwargs)[source]¶

Email subscribers and log to /api/approved/ exactly once, when an article becomes approved.

news.signals.restrict_subscriptions(sender, instance, action, reverse, pk_set, **kwargs)[source]¶

Only readers may subscribe, and only to journalists.

Clearing/trimming pk_set during “pre_add” stops Django from adding those rows.

post_migrate handler (connected in apps.py).
